accepted_vs_rejected_finding.accepted_turnaround: The four-view neutral sheet establishes the mature face, ivory shoulder apparatus, diagonal copper route, right-hip module, and heavy right greave with useful front/back clarity, though small construction and hair details drift and the heavy-leg asymmetry is weak in the side views.
accepted_vs_rejected_finding.accepted_weapon: The weapon sheet communicates one long two-hand odachi, base-only caged mineral element, insulated hilt, profile, scabbard, and enlarged guard/grip construction with good 2D design-sheet clarity, while small routing details drift and the blade-base cage remains only visually plausible.
accepted_vs_rejected_finding.rejected_combat_attempts: The initial image has the clearest same-hilt two-hand grasp but deletes the defining shoulder apparatus; revision 01 restores identity but leaves the leading fist hovering off the hilt; revision 02 restores identity but places the trailing hand on a separate copper form and crosses the hilt through the leg silhouette. None is accepted evidence.

benchmark_comparison.method: The private archive was extracted into a random disposable workspace. All 20 unique decodable benchmark visuals were inspected at native resolution; one additional decodable file was an exact visual duplicate. Six relevant character, weapon, and combat comparisons were then built as unlabeled 1600x900 two-panel sheets. Each pair used native sources, framing-only crops where needed, aspect-preserving scale and neutral padding, independently randomized left/right placement, and no retouching. The sheets were judged without provenance labels and destroyed after inspection.

categories.finding: The large identity anchors survive front and back, but side-view heavy-greave proof, braid volume, small brackets, and seam logic are not fully locked.

Four complete neutral views share a baseline, scale, readable hands, and uncropped feet; imperfect orthographic consistency and weak side-view asymmetry keep it below a top production preflight sheet.
The accepted neutral body is mature, weight-bearing, and proportionally credible, while the rejected combat hands show that anatomy is not reliably preserved under pose pressure.
The face is mature and specific with stable overall identity; eye, hairline, braid placement, and braid volume drift enough across views and combat attempts to prevent premium lock.
Ivory, cobalt, copper, and blackened steel separate cleanly, but the layering remains simple industrial workwear with attached hardware rather than premium mythic-anime AAA costume authorship.
The shoulder apparatus and heavy grounding leg create a distinct functional asymmetry, yet the overall read remains closer to a science-fiction field technician than an apex mythic combat lead.

No accepted combat-grip image exists. The only clearly two-handed rejected attempt omits the defining shoulder identity; the identity-preserving revisions leave one hand off the hilt or on a separate element.
The blade, long hilt, profile, scabbard, and grip construction are visually coherent, but base-cage stresses, mass balance, fastener continuity, and copper routing remain unresolved visual proposals.
The pack avoids fetish anatomy, heels, glossy plastic, and direct franchise mimicry, but the cobalt work suit and bolt-on industrial modules retain a generic civilian-technician ceiling.
The work is clean and distinctive as science-fiction concept art, but it lacks the benchmark's iconic mythic hierarchy, authored costume storytelling, weapon-body integration, and combat force.

decision.biggest_remaining_gap: The absence of one accepted identity-preserving combat image that unambiguously proves both complete hands closed on separated regions of the same hilt.
